ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and individuals with 25%+ control against (i) the consolidated Canadian sanctions list administered by Global Affairs Canada under SEMA/SIMSA and the Magnitsky Act; (ii) the Criminal Code List of Terrorist Entities; (iii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; and (iv) the US OFAC SDN List, which is contractually mandatory given USD SWIFT and ACH payment corridors. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), as defined in the PCMLTFA, and their family members and close associates must undergo enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds verification, and all findings must be documented and retained for at least five years. FINTRAC large virtual currency transaction and suspicious transaction reporting obligations are assessed; for a passive programmatic ad-exchange LP, no FINTRAC registration is triggered absent money-services business activities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online / BC Registry Services (bcregistry.ca) operated by the Registrar of Companies, Service BC
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The entity name must be in English or French using Latin-alphabet characters. A BC limited partnership name must end with 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 'LP' (or the French equivalents 'Société en commandite' / 'S.E.C.'). Foreign corporate names submitted for registration must be translated or transliterated and a statutory declaration of translation/transliteration filed. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing name, trademark, or registered BC entity, per s. 28 of the BC Business Corporations Act and BC partnership name guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: a valid BC name approval may be extended once for an additional 56 days by filing a name approval extension request through BC Corporate Online before the original approval expires, subject to the applicable statutory fee. Rejection appeal: there is no statutory merits appeal specific to name refusals; the applicant must submit a written Request for Reconsideration to the Deputy Registrar of Companies within 30 days of refusal, addressing the examiner's confusion note with distinguishing arguments and, for sensitive tokens, attaching the relevant regulator's written consent (e.g., OFSI consent for 'Bank'/'Trust'/'Insurance'). If reconsideration fails, the applicant may file a fresh name request with an alternate name or file a petition for judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only when the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address within British Columbia, is staffed during normal business hours, and accepts service of process. A P.O. Box or mail-forwarding-only address is non-compliant for registration of a BC limited partnership. A registered-agent service with records-retention capability satisfies CRA's books-and-records location requirement for this low-risk AdTech holding platform.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% annualized probability). The BC Registrar conducts no routine physical inspections of registered offices. CRA on-site visits are rare for a non-licensed digital advertising principal, and generally occur only upon a GST/HST or income tax audit trigger. FINTRAC examinations apply only if the entity registers as a reporting entity, which is not anticipated for a passive SSP/Ad Exchange platform.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a British Columbia limited partnership; no escrow or capital deposit is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement to govern the Partnership, including capital contributions, profit-sharing, and management powers. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Partnership’s registered office shall be as set forth in the Application for Registration, and the designated representative is authorized to file same with BC Registries. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial general partner appoints [name] as Compliance and Registered Office Contact, and authorizes the opening of bank accounts and the execution of such standard documents as may be required to commence business operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Name Request via BC Corporate Online or BC Registry paper service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS or BC Registry name search for the proposed limited partnership name. Submit a Name Reservation Request to confirm the name is distinguishable from existing corporate and personal property security records. The reservation is valid for 56 days.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Request Form
NUANS or BC Registry Name Search Report
General Partner’s written consent to use the proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, amend the flagged words and resubmit a fresh name request; if the objection relates to confusing similarity, the proponent may provide evidence of consent from the registered owner or appeal to the Registrar within the applicable review period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal legal counsel and the partners; no government filing is required at this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a Limited Partnership Agreement among the general partner and limited partners, setting out capital commitments, profit and loss allocations, management authority, transfer restrictions, and dissolution procedures. The executed agreement must be retained for registry inspection and banking KYC purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Schedule of general and limited partners with initial capital contributions
General Partner’s corporate formation documents and officer list if it is a body corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If material defects are identified before filing, the partners may rescind and re-execute the agreement by supplemental amendment; any signed counterpart that would conflict with the filed application must be superseded by unanimous consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Limited Partnership Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries, Ministry of Finance, via Corporate Online or paper submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form LP-A with the required particulars, including the limited partnership name, registered office address in British Columbia, name and address of the general partner, and confirmation of the liability of limited partners. Pay the statutory filing fee and obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Form LP-A Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Registered Office Notice or consent of the registered office address
General Partner’s resolution authorizing registration
Name reservation certificate, if obtained
Statutory filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by BC Registries, respond in writing within the requested deadline to correct minor discrepancies; if the application is rejected, amend the form and resubmit, paying the refiling fee if such fee is assessed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for Federal and Provincial Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) at www.canada.ca/business-registration; BC Ministry of Finance for PST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a CRA Business Number and register for GST/HST and, if the partnership has employees, a payroll account. Register for PST with the BC Ministry of Finance if taxable supplies are made. These registrations are completed online using the business registry platform.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Limited Partnership Agreement
Legal name and business contact information
Identification and authorization for the general partner and its officers
CRA Request for Business Number and account registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or returns the registration, correct the mismatch in legal name, business number, or partner details and resubmit; contact the CRA Business Registration line for manual validation if online filing is denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City or municipal licensing office (e.g., City of Vancouver Business Licence and Regulatory Services), municipal fire department, and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the limited partnership maintains physical commercial premises, apply for the applicable municipal business license. Arrange for fire safety inspection, building occupancy permit, and compliance with British Columbia Building Code requirements. If employees will be engaged, register the employer with WorkSafeBC.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Lease or proof of premises
Floor plan and building occupancy documents
Fire safety inspection checklist or certificate
WorkSafeBC employer registration application, if applicable
Municipal business license application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an inspection identifies deficiencies, correct the violations and schedule a re-inspection; if the municipal license is denied, the applicant may appeal to the board of variance or the applicable municipal licensing tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Institution of Banking and Payment Rail Access
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian bank or authorized financial institution providing ACH and SWIFT services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Canadian corporate bank account in the name of the limited partnership by presenting the Certificate of Limited Partnership, Limited Partnership Agreement, and the General Partner’s board resolution. Complete AML/KYC declarations identifying beneficial owners and set up ACH and SWIFT payment rails.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Limited Partnership Agreement
General Partner’s board resolution authorizing bank account opening
Certified identification for the general partner and authorized officers
Beneficial ownership and source of funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC or AML queries, provide an updated organizational chart, certified beneficial ownership details, and a narrative explanation of funding sources; escalate to the institution’s compliance officer or select another Schedule I bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no provincial industrial licensing board regulates a programmatic advertising exchange; a municipal business license may apply if physical office premises are maintained.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industry-specific operating license is required for NAICS 541810 programmatic real-time ad exchange and SSP services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: BC Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (Environmental Protection Division)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no manufacturing, physical discharge, or land disturbance; no Environmental Impact Assessment required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital advertising operations; general municipal wastewater, waste handling, and e-waste disposal bylaws must be observed if office hardware is used.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical commercial premises: obtain fire safety certification, occupancy permit, structural load inspection approval, egress compliance under the BC Building Code, and, if employees are engaged, register with WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada - portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial authorities: BC Registries and Online Services (Limited Partnership registration under the BC Partnership Act) and BC Ministry of Finance Provincial Tax Administration via eTaxBC (BC PST).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Register the Limited Partnership under British Columbia law at the BC Corporate Registry via OneStop Business Registry to obtain the BC LP registration number and legal existence. STEP 2: Apply to the CRA for the federal Business Number (BN) and the GST/HST program account (RT) using Form RC1 or the joint federal-provincial business registration service; the Canadian-resident general partner signs the application, and non-resident partners are identified through the CRA non-resident registration process. STEP 3: Register for BC PST through eTaxBC immediately before the first taxable sale in British Columbia; BC PST has no small-supplier threshold exemption. STEP 4: Open payroll program accounts (RP/RC) only if the LP employs Canadian staff; not required for a pure pass-through AdTech holding platform without payroll. STEP 5: File the annual T5013 partnership information return within five months of the partnership fiscal year-end and issue T5013 slips to all partners; partnership income is computed at the LP level and flows through to partners for their respective tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - a BC Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act s. 96(1); the LP itself pays no federal Part I income tax and no BC corporate income tax. Income, gains, and losses are allocated to partners in their agreed proportions. Non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are taxable in Canada on their share of Canadian-source partnership business income (ITA ss. 2(3) and 96(4)), subject to treaty relief. For GST/HST, the LP is deemed a separate person (Excise Tax Act s. 272.1(2)) and must register once its worldwide taxable supplies exceed the small-supplier threshold. Territorial scope: only income attributable to the Canadian business conducted through the LP is subject to Canadian taxation; the passive foreign income of non-resident partners is generally outside Canadian taxing jurisdiction. The entity-level SIFT Partnership rules are inapplicable because the LP is privately held and not publicly traded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no elective check-the-box regime; partnership classification is fixed by statute. The following elections are available to a BC LP engaged in AdTech export services: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration before the CAD $30,000 threshold under ETA s. 240(2) to recover input tax credits; (ii) election to file GST/HST separately from the calendar year or to file annually for qualifying registrants; (iii) election for a non-calendar partnership fiscal period under ITA s. 249.1(7) where all partners are non-residents; (iv) allocation of income by the partners' agreed proportions in the limited partnership agreement (ITA s. 96(1)); (v) no hybrid mismatch election exists - proposed ITA ss. 18.2 and 18.3 (hybrid mismatch rules) are not yet in force, and a U.S. partner's own check-the-box election classifying the Canadian LP as opaque may trigger recharacterization by the CRA under the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s. 245) or under the Canada-US Tax Treaty business-profits article.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST (value-added goods and services tax at 5%) administered by the CRA, supplemented in British Columbia by the provincial PST (retail sales tax at 7%) administered by the BC Ministry of Finance on enumerated taxable goods and specific taxable software licences. Combined nominal indirect burden is 12% on PST-taxable supplies, but programmatic advertising exchange, DSP, and SSP platform services supplied to business customers are generally non-taxable services under the BC PST and are subject only to 5% GST. Standard B2B domestic supply of digital advertising services is taxable at 5% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD $30,000 - GST/HST small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1), measured on the worldwide taxable supplies of the LP and its associated persons in the current calendar quarter and the immediately preceding four calendar quarters; crossing this threshold triggers mandatory GST/HST registration, collection, and remittance. BC PST: no registration threshold; a seller must register via eTaxBC before making any taxable sale in BC, including the licensing of standardized commercial software used in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, state-run API validation, or digital stamping for GST/HST invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted and voluntarily standardized through the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing (Peppol) framework. Every registrant must issue a GST/HST invoice containing the supplier's legal name and Business Number, date of issue, description of the supply, and either the GST/HST charged or a clear statement that the supply is zero-rated; invoices may be issued and stored electronically. All accounting records and export substantiation must be retained in readable format for six years (ETA s. 286) and produced to the CRA upon demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Programmatic AdTech DSP/SSP services qualify for the 0% GST/HST rate as a supply of a service to a non-resident person under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, provided that the service is not rendered to an individual physically present in Canada at the time of performance, does not relate to real property situated in Canada, and does not relate to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance unless that property is exported. The non-resident status of the counterparty must be evidenced by its ordinary business address, tax residence documentation, and payment origin; the computer servers executing programmatic bids may be located globally, but the benefit, use, and consumption of the service must rest with the non-resident recipient outside Canada. Mixed-purpose contracts covering both Canadian and foreign campaign delivery must clearly allocate the Canadian portion to taxable supplies and the foreign portion to zero-rated supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Export Declaration (eManifest/GCA export reporting) for any physical goods export component, if applicable
Bill of Lading (ocean or air waybill) or equivalent electronic proof of export for goods movements
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of payment from the non-resident counterparty
Executed digital services agreement identifying the non-resident recipient's legal name, registered address, and country of tax residence
Commercial invoice expressly citing ETA Schedule VI Part V s. 7 with the notation GST/HST: 0% zero-rated export of services
Server and IP routing logs or platform delivery reports demonstrating that the advertising service is consumed outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess a zero-rated export supply within four years of the assessment date, extended to seven years where misrepresentation, negligence, or fraud is established. Failure to substantiate the non-resident recipient or the foreign consumption of the service results in full reversal of the zero-rating and reassessment of 5% GST on the gross consideration, plus prescribed interest (currently above 9% per annum for corporate arrears). Statutory penalties include: ETA s. 280(1) failure-to-collect penalty of 10% of the tax not collected, ETA s. 280(1.1) failure-to-file penalty of 5% of the net tax plus 1% per full month of delinquency to a maximum of 12 months, and ETA s. 285 knowing or grossly negligent false statement penalty of 25% of the understated net tax. The CRA cross-matches the commercial contract, invoice, bank remittance records, and platform IP logs; discrepancies such as Canadian billing addresses, Canadian campaign geo-targeting, or domestic consumption of the service will rebut the zero-rating claim and trigger a full clawback. Intentional fraudulent export schemes may also attract the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA s. 245) and criminal exposure under the Criminal Code. For non-resident partners, any reassessed GST/HST liability of the partnership is jointly and severally enforceable against each partner under ETA s. 272.1(3).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the monetary authority and operator of the high-value settlement system (Lynx, formerly LVTS). Canada maintains no centralized foreign-exchange control ministry; prudential regulation of banks is vested in the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and transaction-level monitoring is undertaken by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Payment service providers, including fintech clearing agents, must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) for activity initiated after the applicable registration deadlines.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a fully convertible free-floating currency. Canada abolished formal exchange controls in the 1950s and imposes no balance-of-payments restrictions, no investment-approval requirement on inward capital, and no restriction on the repatriation of capital, dividends, or partnership distributions. Both current-account items (exported advertising-technology services, software licensing, global bid-stream royalties) and capital-account items (limited-partner contributions, shareholder loans, return of capital) may be denominated and settled in CAD or any freely convertible foreign currency. The practical profit-remittance friction is exclusively tax-driven for the BC Limited Partnership (LP): Canadian-source business income must be allocated on a flow-through basis to each partner via T5013 schedules and, where a partner is a non-resident, the non-resident must either file a Canadian Part I tax return or rely on treaty-relief forms (NR301/NR302), because the partnership is not subject to Part XIII withholding on business-income distributions per se but must comply with the CRA administrative withholding and reporting regime for non-resident partners. GST/HST on exported advertising services is normally zero-rated with input-credit eligibility, removing VAT as a cash-flow hurdle. No exchange-control license or central-bank permission is required for any transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender regime. There is no requirement for an exporter of services to convert, repatriate, escrow, or deposit foreign-currency receivables into CAD with the Bank of Canada, and no mandatory conversion ratio or statutory timeline applies to export receipts. The BC LP may freely retain USD, EUR, and other currencies in foreign-currency operating accounts at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The only relevant obligations are: (i) FINTRAC reporting for cross-border wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more (or foreign-currency equivalent) under the PCMLTFA; (ii) accurate invoicing and source-of-funds documentation supporting the commercial purpose of each receivable from foreign ad exchanges and DSP/SSP counterparties; and (iii) documentation of foreign-currency gains or losses for income-tax purposes where the LP adopts a Canadian-dollar functional currency or elects to report in USD.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a supplementary collection corridor, LOW as a primary treasury rail. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) licensed under, for example, the UK FCA EMI regime or EU electronic-money directives are not recognized by OSFI as Canadian deposit-taking institutions and cannot provide a Canadian bank account, a CAD IBAN-equivalent clearing number, or direct membership in Payments Canada's Lynx, ACSS, or Real-Time Rail (RTR) settlement systems. A BC LP may lawfully use an offshore EMI only to collect USD/EUR/GBP receivables from foreign advertisers and publishers provided: (i) the EMI is properly registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC if it solicits Canadian clients; (ii) the LP itself remains the regulated PSP for Canadian payment-taking (RPAA registration); and (iii) all EMI balances are swept daily to the LP's Schedule I Canadian bank account to avoid unregistered foreign-money-services exposure and to preserve CAD clearing capability. As a primary rail, an offshore EMI fails because it cannot originate CAD ACH debits, cannot clear Canadian payroll, and creates FINTRAC double-reporting risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian FINTRAC regulations do not categorically mandate an in-branch interview; however, the Big Five banks operating in British Columbia uniformly require, in practice, either (a) a physical visit by the account's authorized signatory (for an LP, the designated representative of the corporate general partner, typically its CFO or director) to a BC branch, or (b) a banker-initiated video interview conducted from an established Canadian branch plus notarized and apostilled corporate documentation. Pure remote opening with zero Canadian nexus is generally rejected by tier-1 banks. In all cases, the LP must provide the Certificate of Limited Partnership from the BC Registry, the partnership agreement, and FINTRAC-required identity verification of every limited partner holding a 25% or greater economic interest, including non-resident partners; documents for non-resident principals must be original passports or certified true copies plus a notarized statement of source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: LP contains non-resident limited partners, especially from lower-tax or secrecy jurisdictions, and the bank cannot readily determine all 25%+ interest holders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full-executed Limited Partnership Agreement; BC Registry Certificate of LP Registration; capital account schedule; an organizational/UBO chart identifying every partner above the 25% threshold with passport copies; tax-residency certificates from each partner's home tax authority; source-of-wealth statements; signed declarations that all contributed funds arise from legitimate commercial or investment activity; and a written indemnity/undertaking to disclose any future partner changes within 15 days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Programmatic adtech payment-flow anonymization: bank identifies DSP-to-SSP-to-publisher money movement as unverifiable, with potential ad-fraud or disciplined 'ghost inventory' concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed framework agreements with recognized ad exchanges (e.g., Google Ad Manager, Magnite, Index Exchange, PubMatic) or direct SSP/DSP standard contracts; monthly publisher payout manifests linking payment amounts to impression/bid-stream reports; proof-of-delivery logs from ad servers; IAB Tech Lab supply-chain object (seller.json/app-ads.txt) attestations; anti-fraud policy and traffic-quality vendor report; ban on cash or cryptocurrency settlement; whitelist of verified publisher bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border wires: monthly inbound and outbound SWIFT traffic from multiple jurisdictions, many individual wires approaching or exceeding CAD 10,000, triggering FINTRAC reporting and potential pattern-of-transaction scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly completed corporate AML program with a designated AML compliance officer, training records, and risk assessment; underlying commercial invoices, purchase orders, or net-30/net-60 media-buy statements; SWIFT MT103 copies for major transactions; a transaction-rationale memo mapping each wire to a named advertiser, campaign, or publisher; and voluntary FINTRAC STR filings made in the ordinary course to demonstrate good-faith compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office/registered-office mismatch: LP uses only a BC registered-office service address while all substantive operations and principals are outside Canada, causing account-refusal risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of substantive BC presence or intent: executed premises lease or sublease; BC Business Number and BC corporate-tax registrations; documentation of Canadian personnel, local director(s), or a local outsourced CFO/administrator; physical address verification letter from the landlord; and a board/general-partner resolution designating a BC-based compliance contact and records location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned/high-risk counterparty leakage: programmatic inventory may include traffic from or payments to entities in OFAC/DFATD/UN-sanctioned jurisdictions or state-sponsored media, and the bank requires demonstrable screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written jurisdiction-screening and geographic-blocking policy; automated OFAC/DFATD screening reports of the supply-chain counterparty list produced quarterly; contractual representations from SSP/DSP partners excluding sanctioned inventory; evidencing of IP-address blocklists; a remediation protocol for any flagged hit; and a copy of the LP's voluntary undertaking to terminate any counterparty appearing on a sanctions list within 24 hours.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Limited-partner capital contributions should be wired by SWIFT MT103 with the remittance narrative (Field 70) stating 'LIMITED PARTNER CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT DATED [date] - NON-RESIDENT INVESTMENT' and, if applicable, the corresponding purpose/function code used by the sending institution. The receiving Schedule I bank will request: the capital-call notice issued by the general partner, a certified excerpt of the LPA establishing the contribution obligation, identity/source-of-funds documentation for the remitting partner, and, for contributions exceeding CAD 10,000, the bank will file a FINTRAC Large Cash or International Electronic Funds Transfer Report (IEFTR). No Bank of Canada or government approval is required because Canada does not operate a capital-control regime; the contribution should be booked as an increase in each partner's capital account and excluded from income. If the contribution is in USD, it may be credited to the LP's USD account and converted to CAD on a spot basis; an election under the Income Tax Act may be made to offset foreign-currency gains on the capital contribution, but the LP's reporting currency and hedge relationship must be documented.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The LP should structure settlement rails in three layers: (i) domestic CAD disbursements to Canadian publishers and vendors via Payments Canada ACSS/EFT or the Lynx high-value wire system for amounts above the EFT cap; (ii) USD disbursements to US-based publishers via the Schedule I bank's US correspondent network using Fedwire or same-bank ACH, or SWIFT MT103 for foreign USD payees; and (iii) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for non-USD international payees, using the ISO 20022 pain.001/MT103 formats to include full remittance mapping (invoice number, campaign ID, publisher ID). For physical-media and out-of-home programmatic follow-ons requiring documentary trade settlement, commercial letters of credit governed by UCP 600 are available; however, standard programmatic RTB ad settlement is executed on net-30 or net-60 credit terms through ACH/SWIFT rather than LCs. For recurring low-value publisher payouts of less than CAD 100,000 per month, Payments Canada's new Real-Time Rail provides immediate ISO 20022 clearing, while Lynx remains the final and irrevocable high-value rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX spot contracts for CAD/USD and cross-currency working-capital conversion
Deliverable FX forwards (tenors up to 12-24 months) executed under an ISDA 1998 FX Master Agreement or Canadian Bankers' Association FX Master Agreement with a Schedule I dealing desk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., INR, CNY, BRL, TRY, KRW) where convertibility restrictions prevent physical delivery and USD cash settlement is required
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-dated USD/CAD revenue alignment and capital-funding optimization
FX vanilla options, zero-cost collars, and knock-out forward structures provided by OSFI-regulated dealing banks
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures and options listed on the TMX Montreal Exchange for standardized mark-to-market hedging with recorded hedge accounting under IFRS 9

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general corporate rate (Federal 15% + British Columbia 12%); 11% combined small business rate for qualifying CCPC partners (Federal 9% + BC 2%). The BC Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent under ITA s. 96; tax is imposed at the partner level on allocated income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credits up to 35% refundable for eligible CCPC software research and development expenditures; BC Innovative Clean Energy and BC Interactive Digital Media Tax Credit (17.5% refundable on qualifying BC labour) for qualifying digital media products, which generally excludes B2B AdTech exchange software; BC small business rate of 2% for a CCPC corporate partner on its share of active business income from the LP.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return; filed via CRA-certified tax software using the Internet File Transfer (EFT/e-file) portal; mandatory electronic filing applicable to partnerships issuing more than 50 T5013 slips.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the fifth month after the partnership fiscal year-end; a partnership with a corporate partner must adopt a calendar fiscal year, making the deadline May 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the BC Limited Partnership, provincial registry number, CRA Business Number, fiscal year-end, and mailing address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register the LP for a CRA Business Number; attach the full name, address, jurisdiction of residence, and percentage interest of every non-resident limited and general partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from programmatic real-time ad exchange, SSP and DSP platform fees, data services and auction transaction revenue, less platform operating expenses (media costs, data, cloud hosting, commissions) to compute aggregate net income or loss under ITA s. 96.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Canadian-source business income to each non-resident partner on the T5013 slips; the non-resident partner remains taxable under Part I and must file a Canadian T1 or T2 return reporting the allocated income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership share of income/loss, capital gains, investment income, and adjusted cost base for each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue a T5013 slip to every non-resident partner and identify each partner as treaty-resident; ensure no Part XIII-tainted items (dividends, interest, royalties) embedded in distributions are left unreported.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); gross negligence civil penalty of 50% of any misstatement; additional penalties apply where required slips contain false statements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (required for a corporate general partner or a corporate limited partner carrying on business through the LP); filed through CRA E-File using certified software; mandatory e-filing for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1 million.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within six months of the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance of tax due within two months (three months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal corporate name, jurisdiction of incorporation, CRA Business Number, NAICS 541810, fiscal year-end, and total worldwide revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate general partner must disclose its foreign jurisdiction, list its LP profit share as Canadian business income, and attach the T5013 partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part I Tax – Taxable Income and Schedule 1
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting the partnership's allocated net income; federal tax at 15% general rate, or 9% small business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for a qualifying CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporate partner is taxed at the 15% federal rate on its share of the LP's Canadian business income and is not eligible for the small business deduction; treaty relief does not eliminate Part I business income tax where the income is attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: BC Provincial Tax Calculation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: British Columbia provincial tax at 12% general rate (2% small business rate for qualifying CCPC); application of provincial tax credits and the BC income allocation formula.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate partner with a permanent establishment in BC, apportion and allocate BC-source income using the BC allocation schedule; the BC 12% rate applies to allocated taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; for a second or subsequent offence: 10% plus 2% per full month up to 24 months; arrears interest on unpaid balance due; 50% gross negligence penalty for false entries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NR4 Statement of Amounts Paid or Credited to a Non-Resident and Part XIII summary return; filed via the CRA NR4 portal; annual return and partner slips.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual NR4 return and partner statements due the last day of March following the calendar year; Part XIII withholding remitted to the CRA by the 15th day of the month following the month in which the amount was paid or credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 14 – Gross Income Paid or Credited
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report Part XIII-tainted payments made by the LP or its corporate general partner to non-residents, including interest, royalties, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ordinary profit allocations to non-resident partners are not reported on NR4; they are reported on T5013 and taxed under Part I. NR4 is required only for payments retaining a Part XIII character, such as royalties paid by the LP for licensed ad-serving technology.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicator fields for treaty-reduced rates and attached NR301, NR302, or NR303 certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the applicable treaty form and a Tax Residence Certificate from the home jurisdiction to invoke relief; failing to certify results in the statutory 25% withholding and possible payer liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file NR4 slips: CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per return); failure to withhold Part XIII: payer assessed the full unwithheld tax, penalty of 10% (first) or 20% (repeat) of the unwithheld amount plus daily compound interest.
